question.text: Which of the following asset classes is known for providing the best liquidity (ease of converting to cash)?

explanation.text: The Logic: Liquidity is the ease and speed with which an asset can be converted into cash with little or no loss in value. Money held in a bank savings account is essentially "cash on call" — it can be withdrawn instantly through ATM, branch, UPI or net-banking with no penalty and no negotiation on value, which is the textbook definition of high liquidity. Real estate transactions take weeks or months to find a buyer, complete documentation and receive funds. Gold jewellery is saleable but typically attracts making-charge loss and dealer discounts, reducing realisable value. A 5-year bank FD is contractually locked, and premature withdrawal involves a penalty and lower interest. The Trap: Real estate and gold jewellery store value but cannot be converted to cash on demand. A long-tenor FD has scheduled liquidity at maturity, not on-demand liquidity. None of these match the immediacy of a savings account. Note: A direct comparison ranking bank savings account ahead of real estate, gold jewellery and a 5-year FD on liquidity is not stated on the cited NISM Series V-B MFF workbook pages checked (pp.12, 13, 14, 31), which define liquidity, note real-estate illiquidity, and mention penalties/charges. The ranking above reflects general industry/regulatory understanding of liquidity across these asset classes rather than the cited workbook chapter.
